premise: A modern protagonist wakes up inside an 1873 Kansas saloon and accidentally spills a gunfighter's whiskey. The gunfighter challenges them to a duel outside. The narration covers historical gunfights, revolvers, quick-draw myths, shooting accuracy and reaction times. The smartest survival strategy: walk back inside and buy the gunfighter another drink.

historicalNotes.status: Research notes to verify against cited sources before the narration is written (CLAUDE.md: fact-check the story).
notes: Revolvers in Kansas around 1873 included cap-and-ball Colts and their cartridge conversions, the Smith & Wesson Model 3 and Remingtons; the Colt Single Action Army was brand new in 1873.
Holsters rode fairly high on the belt; the low, tied-down quick-draw holster is largely a 20th-century film convention. Many men carried a pistol in a coat pocket or waistband.
Wide-brim, high-crowned felt hats (the 1865 Stetson 'Boss of the Plains' style) and bowlers were both common; avoid later Hollywood hat shapes and heavy fringe.
Several Kansas cattle towns had ordinances against carrying firearms in town, which the story may want to acknowledge.
